title: Fall Back! Daylight Saving Time Ends on November 1
summary:
On November 1, 2026, many people in North America will turn their clocks back one hour. This ends Daylight Saving Time, or DST, which began on March 8, 2026. The change gives more sunlight in the morning during the shorter winter days.

DST started during World War I. In 1916, the German Empire moved clocks forward to save fuel, and the US and Britain soon did the same. It came back in World War II. After 1945, different US places used different dates. By 1965, Iowa alone had 23 sets of dates! The Uniform Time Act of 1966 set the same dates for the country, but Hawaii, most of Arizona and some US territories do not take part.

About 70 countries use DST, but experts say changing clocks can disturb sleep. The House passed the Sunshine Protection Act by 308-117 in July 2026 to make DST permanent, but the Senate has not approved it yet. For now, enjoy the extra hour!
why_it_matters: The clock change affects everyone's sleep and daily schedule, so knowing the date helps families get ready for the shorter winter days.

background_read: Daylight Saving Time moves clocks forward in spring so the evening stays light longer, then back again in autumn.
Countries first used the idea during wartime to save fuel by needing less artificial light.
Today governments still debate whether changing the clocks twice a year is helpful or harmful.
